title: Subsurface scattering breaks MSAA/causes bleedthrough between transparent and opaque objects
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e] ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.5001) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory ### Issue description Hi! I've got a slightly long winded bug today, where subsurface scattering breaks MSAA between transparent, and opaque objects The setup for this bug is as follows: 1. You need an object which enters the transparency pipeline. In this test case, this is achieved via a depth buffer read via a shader 2. You also need another visible object which has subsurface scattering enabled 3. MSAA then breaks between objects which are opaque, and objects which are in the transparency pipeline. This also causes visual glitches with the subsurface scattering effect This results in a pixel thin halo effect between opaque and transparent objects, which is the skybox bleeding through. Opaque <-> opaque MSAA is unaffected. To illustrate this, the big blue 'water' plane (ClipmapHigh) has a shader which performs a depth buffer read to push it into the transparency pipeline. The green tree has subsurface scattering enabled. Here's what the difference in settings looks like: Bugged: The tree has subsurface scattering enabled, water is in the transparency pipeline: Works fine: The tree is hidden, water is in the transparency pipeline: Works fine: The tree has subsurface scattering enabled, water is *not* in the transparency pipeline (remove line 13 from water.gdshader): Disabling subsurface scattering (under tree_with_subsurface_scattering.tscn) also fixes the problem instead of hiding the tree. This bug is also affected by frustrum culling of subsurface scattered objects MSAA 2x-8x is affected equally, and the problem does not occur if MSAA is disabled. It reproduces under both vulkan and d3d12. I'm on an AMD GPU, and I do not know if it reproduces under Nvidia There's a few other bugs which bring up issues with subsurface scattering - but I've been unable to tell if they're strictly related. I strongly suspect this is the cause of at least a few issues that have been reported around subsurface scattering, but it can be hard to spot because MSAA only fails between opaque and transparent objects. Its a lot more subtle in real scenes, and may look solely like its a bug in the subsurface scattering - eg the odd banding here is caused by the same problem: MSAA continues to work correctly between objects that are opaque and rendered on top of each other, which also significantly obfuscates the problem: Hopefully this is helpful! If you need any more information, testing, or I've stuffed anything up, please let me know and I'll get on it 👍 ### Steps to reproduce This issue is visible in the editor on startup, or run the scene main.tscn and observe the camera Toggle the visibility of the tree "subsurface_scattering_tree" to observe the change in halo effect, or disable subsurface scattering in tree_with_subsurfacescattering.tscn The water can be removed from the transparency pipeline by commenting out line 13 of water.gdshader ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) https://github.com/20k/godot_bug1 or as a zip: [bug-transparency.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26481318/bug-transparency.zip)
